chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Dhubyan ibn Hakim al-Awadi from Musa ibn Uqayl from Dawud ibn al-Husayn said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When you bear witness to a testimony and wish to establish it, alter it however you wish, arrange it, and correct it to the best of your ability until the matter becomes valid for the owner of the right, provided that you do not testify except with his right and do not add to the essence of the right that which is not his right. For indeed the witness nullifies the right and validates the right, and by the witness the right is established and by the witness the right is given. And for the witness, in establishing the testimony by correcting it with everything he can find a way to, from adding words, meanings, and explanation in the testimony, that by which he establishes and validates the right, and it is not taken as an addition to the right, such as the reward of the fasting person, the standing one, the one striving with his sword in the way of Allah.'
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for a witness correcting or rephrasing their testimony in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In the Shia jurisprudential tradition, this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that a witness is not merely a passive recorder but an active agent in establishing rights (*thubut al-haqq*). It permits the witness to rephrase, rearrange, and elaborate on their testimony to ensure clarity and validity for the right-holder, provided they do not add anything extraneous to the right itself, such as adding the reward of a fasting person to the testimony of a fighter. This principle underscores the witness's role in ensuring the legal truth is fully realized and protected.
